key_insight: Physics-informed and data-driven neural operators can both model dynamic wall-slip Couette flow, but DeepONet is the practical choice for fast, reusable prediction across parameters.
engineering_relevance: This work points to surrogate models that can enable near-real-time fluid dynamics forecasting and rapid parametric studies for flow-control and design applications.
method: PINN solves the governing Couette-flow equations for fixed physical parameters
DeepONet is trained on high-fidelity Crank-Nicolson data to learn the solution operator across slip and wall-speed conditions
Models are compared on accuracy, generalization, and inference speed
evidence_signal: The PINN reached 0.083% relative L2 error, while DeepONet achieved 0.36% mean relative error on unseen cases and 0.88% on out-of-distribution signals, with about 540X speedup over the numerical solver.
watch_item: The PINN is accurate but requires instance-specific retraining, which limits deployment for changing boundary conditions or parameter sweeps.
paper_title: Solution of the Newtonian plane Couette flow with dynamic wall slip using machine-learning methods
